acceptanceCriteria: A batch form (for example `ticket refine --batch --payload-stdin` taking `[{target, expectedRevision, payload}]`) validates every entry before writing and applies them in bounded chunks, releasing the writer lock between chunks.
Each entry keeps its own CAS check and receipt; a failed entry is reported per entry and does not partially apply that entry; the result lists every entry's outcome.
Replay with the same request id is idempotent (CAL-V0-065 style).
Maintained tests cover all-success, one stale expectedRevision, malformed entry rejected before any write, and a claim committing between chunks.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#625 (orchestrator triage; reporter observations on main-2fff511, not reproduced yet).

Applying the same refine to 110 tickets took about 45 min (one CAS transaction per ticket) and starved claims and heartbeats (LOCK_TIMEOUT, a critical claim PENDING 15 min).

completion.reason: Delivered in PR beamfall/corvint#632, merged to main as 265835f77f9aca1175dfeac06ee7e63ecf17a805. Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-06-v1-0854-batch-refine.md at that commit (the digest is that file's sha256), which records the change, the maintained tests the acceptance criteria name, the independent Codex review and its repairs. The batch head passed the doc gates, go vet, the full suites of the touched packages on darwin and every hosted CI check (go-product shards, doc-gates, go-interop). NOT_RUN: make gate, live multi-agent/dispatcher qualification and non-darwin execution where that entry says so.

title: corvint-tasks: batch ticket mutation (refine many tickets in bounded chunks that yield the store lock) (issue #625)
